brief: Goldman's Soria argues headline indices sit near highs, but under the surface the market rewards quality, driven by higher rates and a forecast growth deceleration across AI and non-AI parts of the economy over the next 12 months, which should favor quality as earnings growth rolls over. Goldman's Quality Pair Index (GSP1QUAL) is up 20% over three months to a 12-month high on about 13% realized volatility, driven mainly by a selloff in the short leg. Quality is negatively correlated to AI, momentum and beta, all crowded (momentum positioning at the 78th percentile of its 5-year range), so Goldman uses it as a hedge and favors quality and defensives over cyclicals, shorting low-quality equities as a cleaner rates trade. The same bias shows within AI: Mag-7 positioning sits at multi-year highs while hyperscaler equities have outperformed their own widening credit spreads. The long-quality, short-momentum pair is up 55% in 2026 after a 60% rout. Technicals are stretched, RSI 83 after 16 of the last 18 sessions up, so Goldman flags a softer CPI print or signs rates are peaking as a reversal trigger, and highlights a call option on the short-leg basket as a hedge against that.
